defects.title: AC-2.2 demands a blocked contract from P2 commands whose gate resolves by default
defects.quote: Gate-trigger run per P2 command: a 7.2 live check with input that hits the gate
defects.what_goes_wrong: AC-2.2 requires worker_done --outcome failed and contract status: blocked for every P2 command, but the rows for auggie-review, cleanup, improve, research, reflect and tasklist resolve their gate by a default or flag (WC-2 a/b), so no input makes them write blocked and the check cannot pass for them.
defects.is_fixed_when: AC-2.2 (or its replacement) states per P2 command, or per resolution type (default, flag, blocked), what the gate-trigger run must produce, and demands failed/status: blocked/blocked_question only for commands whose section 3 row resolves a gate as blocked, with a checkable pass condition for the default-resolving commands.
defects.deletion_note: No: deleting AC-2.2 or the default-resolving rows would drop the gate-conversion test for P2 and the listed behaviour; the fix must keep a gate check for every P2 command.
defects.present_in_others_hint: Section 3.2 rows 88, 100, 103, 110, 116, 122; AC-2.1 and AC-2.4 (the only existing checks for default-resolving rows); WC-2 text; P2 command list at line 160; roadmap (P3, line 118) was mis-listed by one reviewer, ignore it.

defects.title: cli-portify gates always block, so AC-2.3 happy path cannot reach succeeded
defects.quote: each of the three approval gates resolves as blocked with the artifact to review named in the contract
defects.what_goes_wrong: The cli-portify row resolves all three approval gates as blocked, names no flag or default that approves a gate and does not say that --resume counts as approval, so every unattended run ends failed under WC-5 and AC-2.3's single happy-path run with --outcome succeeded cannot pass.
defects.is_fixed_when: The cli-portify row (or AC-2.3) defines how a run reaches succeeded: either a caller-supplied approval input per gate (flag or documented resume semantics saying the resumed run passes the gate named in the contract), or an explicit statement that cli-portify is exempt from the single-run AC-2.3 with its own multi-run check.
defects.deletion_note: No: removing cli-portify from P2 or deleting AC-2.3 for it leaves the command with no way for an unattended run to finish, which is the defect; the fix must state the path to success or an explicit replacement check.
defects.present_in_others_hint: WC-2 (b) and WC-3 (answer-as-flag has no flag for cli-portify); cli-portify resume cell (--resume <contract>); AC-2.2/AC-2.3 at lines 200-201; INV-A:45,79 proposed 'ask or explicit auto-approve flag'.

defects.title: Contract path undefined when the output flag names a file (tdd, init-lite, AC-2.2 example)
defects.quote: where `<output-dir>` is the directory the coordinator passed (`--output` / `--output-dir`)
defects.what_goes_wrong: WC-4 puts return-contract.yaml in the directory the coordinator passed, but the tdd and init-lite rows and the AC-2.2 example pass --output <file>, so no contract directory is defined and 7.2 steps 3-4 (test -s <contract>) have no path to check; spec-panel's added --output has no stated file/dir type either.
defects.is_fixed_when: WC-4 states where the contract goes when the output flag names a file (for example beside it or in a separately named directory flag), and the tdd, init-lite, spec-panel rows and the AC-2.2 example are consistent with that rule.
defects.deletion_note: No: dropping --output <file> or the contract for those commands would remove the report path the coordinator needs (WC-4 'known before dispatch'); the path rule must exist.
defects.present_in_others_hint: Lines 76, 87, 90, 120, 182-183, 200; 'known before dispatch' in WC-4; WC-11 collision when two tdd workers write files into one directory; the spec-panel command definition (command.md) uses a separate --report-dir and is only corroboration, not part of the original spec.

defects.title: Contract location undefined for commands with no output flag (cli-eval, AC-2.2 example)
defects.quote: contract for both pipelines (today a chat table)
defects.what_goes_wrong: The cli-eval row adds a contract but no output flag or directory, so WC-4's '<output-dir> the coordinator passed' has no flag to receive it and AC-2.2's example (cli-eval run --unattended with no --suite) has no contract path to open; the same gap exists for cli-portify (file location unnamed) and other rows that only say 'contract'.
defects.is_fixed_when: Each section 3.2 row that adds a contract either adds an output flag/directory or names its default contract location, and WC-4 says where the contract goes when blocking happens before any directory is parsed (as in the cli-eval missing --suite case).
defects.deletion_note: No: removing the cli-eval contract or its AC-2.2 example would drop the report the coordinator must open; a location must be defined.
defects.present_in_others_hint: Rows 105, 115, 116, 117, 121 in section 3.2; P1 scope text ('output flags for commands that lack one') covers only P1 commands; the audited revised spec added a WC-4 fallback pointing at 'its section 3.1 row', which does not contain cli-eval.

defects.title: 7.2 step 6 git-status check fails for edit-in-place commands on the happy path
defects.quote: **Pass:** only files under the brief's output directory (and the command's documented artifacts) appear.
defects.what_goes_wrong: AC-2.3 applies 7.2 to every P2 happy path, but cleanup, improve, task and cli-portify edit or write product files outside the output directory, and 'documented artifacts' is not defined to include applied edits, so step 6 fails for a correct run unless the implementer assumes it does.
defects.is_fixed_when: Step 6 states what may appear for commands that edit in place (for example exactly the files the contract lists under artifacts, or files the brief authorizes), and 'documented artifacts' is defined.
defects.deletion_note: No: deleting step 6 would remove the check that a worker made no unauthorized change (SA-1/WC-9 support); the pass condition should be narrowed, not removed.
defects.present_in_others_hint: AC-0.4 and AC-1.2 also use 7.2; WC-4 'artifacts' field; rows 103, 105, 107, 109, 110, 121.

defects.title: Claim that no phase makes tdd, troubleshoot and release-split write the contract
defects.quote: the worker reports the named file until Phase 1 adds the contract
defects.what_goes_wrong: Part (b) fails: P1 Scope says the WC-4 contract and the --unattended flag apply to every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2, line 79 says Phase 1 adds the contract to the 3.1 commands, and AC-1.1 asserts each such command has a section naming return-contract.yaml, so the contract is assigned before P2's AC-2.3 (only the P1 Commands cell omits these commands, a cosmetic inconsistency).
defects.is_fixed_when: Not applicable (false positive); a later spec is fine if the P1 scope/AC-1.1 still cover every 3.1 and 3.2 command.
defects.present_in_others_hint: The file-valued --output half of gid 393 is covered by c12-d3.

extra_noticed.title: P1 Commands cell omits 3.1 commands that P1 scope and AC-1.1 cover
extra_noticed.quote: The WC-4 contract in unattended mode; the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2
extra_noticed.what_goes_wrong: The P1 Commands cell lists only some commands (not init-lite, tdd, troubleshoot, release-split), while the Scope cell and AC-1.1 cover all of sections 3.1 and 3.2, so a reader following the Commands cell alone could skip them.
